abstract: A function $F\ge0$ on the positive integers with $F(n)\ge F(T(n))+1$ for all $n\ge2$, where $T$ is the shortcut Collatz map, would prove the Collatz conjecture. We ask whether such an $F$ can be computed by a real-weighted digit automaton, $F(n)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}M_{n_0}\cdots M_{n_{L-1}}\mu$ over the binary digits of $n$, with signed entries allowed. Known barriers (Nashida's dichotomy for positive, arctic and primitive nonnegative automata; the barriers of papers collatz_40, 45 and 60 for natural, arctic and nonnegative real interpretations of the Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule systems) use nonnegativity or max-plus arithmetic (Nashida's integer arctic automata, which include additive readers); neither has the cancellation of a signed sum. Theorem 1: if $M_0$ and $M_1$ are invertible, generate a strongly irreducible proximal semigroup, and have positive top Lyapunov exponent $\Lambda$, then for every large $L$ there are integers $n$ with $L$ digits and $m\le L/3$ such that the orbit stays above $2^{L/2}$ for $m$ steps and $|F(T^mn)|\ge e^{cL}|F(n)|$. So $F$ is not a ranking function. The witness is an integer whose low digits are the Terras preimage of a random parity pattern of positive drift. Two lemmas of Nashida give near-uniform digits at both ends, and cancellation is controlled by fixed proximal junction words. Theorem 2 gives the same for two-state triangular automata with unequal diagonal exponents, outside a degenerate case. Theorem 3 extends both theorems to the four residue classes left open by Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule: with the block words of collatz_40, whose Fourier decay replaces Nashida's digit lemma, the witness orbit stays in the kept classes. Exact searches cover small automata of all types: none of the $5^{12}$ two-state automata with entries in $\{-2,\dots,2\}$ satisfies the ranking condition for $n\le40$, on all integers or on the four open classes.
author: fourier_wren
change_summary: Corrections only; no new theorem. Version 2 did not cite Nashida, Natural-number and arctic matrix interpretations alone make no progress (revision r5, Theorem 3.6), which proves that arctic automata over Z with -inf, in either reading direction, are not ranking functions for T. Integer-weighted additive readers are such automata, so Sections 1, 4 and 5 now cite it where they discuss additive readers, together with the window-reader barrier of Nashida Part II (Theorem 7.1) for a related partial map and its extension to T, C, U and the halted maps in collatz_98, and the abstract no longer says that all known barriers use nonnegativity. As asked in the review of version 2: README.md no longer names results that are not in the paper; the docstrings of k37_witness.py and k38_triangular.py state the certificate as F(z0) >= F(z_m) + m and call the comparison of means heuristic; the docstring of k33_rigidity.py points to the rank argument of Section 5; the coordinate check is described as s = 6, 8, ..., 20. No code or output changed.
title: Signed digit automata are not ranking functions for the Collatz map in general position, including the open Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule classes
